conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states 'Conclusion: Supported' and provides evidence from randomized controlled trials demonstrating that adjunctive cannabidiol reduces convulsive seizure frequency in children with Dravet syndrome.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
**Conclusion: Supported.** High-quality randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trials show that **pharmaceutical, purified cannabidiol used in addition to existing antiseizure treatment** reduces convulsive-seizure frequency in children/adolescents with treatment-resistant Dravet syndrome.

In a 14-week trial of 199 patients aged 2–18, both 10 and 20 mg/kg/day adjunctive cannabidiol reduced convulsive seizures more than placebo (48.7% and 45.7% reductions, respectively, versus 26.9% with placebo). The 10-mg/kg/day dose had a better tolerability profile. An earlier randomized trial in 120 patients also found benefit, supporting reproducibility.

This evidence applies to prescribed cannabidiol oral solution—not over-the-counter CBD products—and to use as an **add-on**, rather than replacement, for established antiseizure medicines. Regulatory labeling also recognizes cannabidiol for seizures associated with Dravet syndrome (FDA indication from age 1; European indication specifies adjunctive use with clobazam from age 2).
